claims.text: Enhanced ethanol oxidation activity and durability are governed by an electron-deficient state of the PGM nanoparticle.
Strong interactions with graphitized N-doped carbon induce the electron-deficient state of the metal nanoparticle.
Cobalt nanoparticles promote transformation of amorphous carbon into highly graphitic carbon.
The graphitic carbon layer is formed in situ during catalyst preparation or operation.
Graphitization stabilizes the catalyst structure through spatial confinement of the PGM nanoparticles.
The starting material contains PGM nanoparticles on an amorphous, N-doped carbon support containing dispersed cobalt nanoparticles.
Removing or replacing cobalt nanoparticles will prevent in situ graphitization of the carbon support.
The proposed mechanism applies to ethanol oxidation in direct ethanol fuel cells.
The relevant structural mediator is a highly graphitic, N-doped carbon layer strongly interacting with the PGM nanoparticle.
The graphitic carbon structure produces a spatial-confinement effect that prevents catalyst structural degradation.
Electronic interactions at the Pd/Co@N-C interface render palladium electron-deficient.
The electron-deficient palladium state enhances electron transfer.
The electron-deficient state improves catalytic activity and durability.
The electron-deficient state makes the 12-electron ethanol oxidation reaction more selective.
Cobalt-containing catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol oxidation currents than otherwise similar cobalt-free catalysts.
Cobalt-containing catalysts will exhibit higher power density and better long-term stability than cobalt-free catalysts.
An inert cobalt-free N-doped carbon baseline will have lower graphitization and a less pronounced electron-deficient PGM state.
This pathway should dominate when ethanol oxidation is the primary reaction.
The pathway may fail for oxygen reduction, different PGM types, or supports that independently alter PGM electronic structure.
Nanoparticle size, dispersion, morphology, and synthesis-dependent support changes may also contribute to performance.
